lines.en: Leo, do you know the painter whose work is in the new exhibition? I admire her a lot.
lines.pt: Leo, você conhece a pintora cuja obra está na nova exposição? Eu a admiro muito.

lines.en: Edith, you mean the artist whose paintings are full of bright colours and old Dublin streets?

lines.en: Yes! She is a woman whose style changed completely after she moved to the coast.

lines.en: I prefer the poet whose book you lent me. He is someone whose words I remember.

lines.en: The writer whose novel won that big prize also studied at my college, so I know his teacher.

lines.en: Then you are a student whose teachers are famous! Is the gallery a place whose entry is free?

lines.en: Yes, the gallery, whose collection grows every year, is free on Sundays.

lines.en: Good. I have a friend whose sister works there as a curator, and she offered us a private tour.

lines.en: Excellent. Let me introduce you to a critic whose reviews are honest and sometimes harsh.

lines.en: A critic whose opinion matters could help me choose a painting for my flat.
lines.pt: Um crítico cuja opinião importa poderia me ajudar a escolher um quadro para o meu apartamento.

lines.en: Then let us go this weekend. Any artist whose work you like can be your guide.
lines.pt: Então vamos neste fim de semana. Qualquer artista cuja obra você goste pode ser seu guia.

facts.label: Whose
facts.sub: Liga pessoa ou coisa ao que é dela: a painter whose work I admire; a gallery whose collection grows. Sem apóstrofo; sem repetir his/her.

facts.label: Cujo/cuja
facts.sub: Use whose + substantivo para ligar uma pessoa ao que ela possui ou fez: a painter whose work I admire. Em português, “cujo” e suas formas; em inglês, whose nunca muda.

facts.label: Cuidado
facts.sub: Whose indica posse; who’s é who is ou who has. Compare: a writer whose book won a prize e a writer who’s famous. O som é igual, mas a escrita não.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: Whose is the same as who’s.
items.why: Who’s means who is or who has.

items.s: Whose is followed by a noun.

answers: Whose shows possession or connection. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
Whose is the same as who’s. → Falso (Who’s means who is or who has.)
Whose is followed by a noun. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)

pages.title: An art room in Dublin · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a quiet Saturday morning in Dublin. Edith and Leo are in a small art room near the river. Paintings in many colours cover the walls. Edith has come here many times before. Leo is looking for a picture for his flat. They talk about the artists they like.

“Leo, do you know the painter whose work is in the new exhibition? I admire her a lot.” says Edith. “Edith, you mean the artist whose paintings are full of bright colours and old Dublin streets?” says Leo. “Yes! She is a woman whose style changed completely after she moved to the coast.” says Edith.
